xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3626: Windows: CLIProxy should auto-install the pinned version (prebuilt win32 binaries do exist)

plan.title: Windows: CLIProxy should auto-install the pinned version (prebuilt win32 binaries do exist)
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: On win32 the CLIProxy auto-installer refuses to install (detectPlatformAsset never learned win32) and the dashboard watchdog throws CliproxyError in a loop for the life of the process. The stated reason is false: CLIProxyAPI v7.2.113 (the pinned version) publishes windows_amd64/windows_aarch64 zip assets containing cli-proxy-api.exe, verified working on Windows 11. Additionally the version probe runs '<bin> --version', a flag v7.2.113 does not define — the binary prints the version banner but exits 2, so the up-to-date check always returns false and every cold start silently redownloads the ~65MB archive on ALL platforms (verified locally on linux).
narratives.Proposal: Add win32 to the asset map (zip extension), make install portable (tar -xf works for both tar.gz via GNU tar and zip via Windows' bundled bsdtar; replace install/rm -rf shell-outs with fs rm->copyFile->chmod), append .exe to the binary path on win32, gate the Unix exec-bit installed-check to non-win32, parse the version banner from stdout even when the probe exits non-zero (all platforms), and replace the bash /dev/tcp sync port probe with netstat parsed in JS on win32. All platform-dependent logic is parameterized (platform = process.platform) for linux-CI unit tests. Full brief: .pan/drafts/PAN-3626.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Skipping or disabling the CLIProxy watchdog on Windows (explicitly rejected by the issue)
- Changing the fuser port-kill fallback in stopCliproxySync/stopCliproxyTask (stays Unix-only behind its silent catch; pid-based kill covers Windows)
- Adding any npm dependency for zip extraction (bsdtar ships with Windows 10 1803+/11)
- Adding a Windows CI runner or CI-run end-to-end Windows install test
- Any upstream CLIProxyAPI changes (e.g. defining a --version flag)
- Changing the probe flag away from --version (undefined flag = banner + fast exit is deliberate)

autoDecisions.summary: Extract both archive types with 'tar -xf' instead of Expand-Archive or a Node unzip library
autoDecisions.rationale: Windows 10 1803+/11 ships bsdtar at System32\tar.exe which extracts zip; GNU tar auto-detects gzip on linux/darwin. One command, zero new dependencies — the issue asked for the simplest portable route.

autoDecisions.summary: Fix the --version probe for all platforms, not just win32
autoDecisions.rationale: Empirically verified during planning: the local linux v7.2.113 binary also prints the banner and exits 2, so isCliproxyUpToDate* is always false and every cold start redownloads the archive on linux/darwin today.

autoDecisions.summary: Keep --version as the probe flag; parse err.stdout on non-zero exit
autoDecisions.rationale: The flag being undefined guarantees the binary prints the banner and exits immediately instead of starting a server; execSync errors and promisified-exec rejections both attach .stdout, so the banner is recoverable.

autoDecisions.summary: Parameterize all new platform-dependent helpers with (platform = process.platform) defaults
autoDecisions.rationale: There is no Windows CI runner; following detectPlatformAsset's existing signature pattern makes every win32 branch unit-testable on linux.

autoDecisions.summary: Replace the bash /dev/tcp fallback with netstat parsed in JS on win32 only
autoDecisions.rationale: bash does not exist on stock Windows so a listening proxy with a stale pidfile reads as down and the CLI spawns a doomed duplicate; parsing netstat output in an exported pure helper avoids fragile findstr quoting and false matches on foreign addresses.

autoDecisions.summary: Install via fs.rm(target) -> copyFile -> chmod instead of the 'install' shell-out
autoDecisions.rationale: GNU install unlinks before writing; naive copyFile over a running binary throws ETXTBSY on linux. chmod 0o755 is harmless on win32. All force-reinstall paths already stop the proxy before installing.

items.title: detectPlatformAsset: map win32 to windows zip assets

expected_outputs: cliproxy-platform-asset.test.ts passes with win32 zip expectations

narrative.Action: In src/lib/cliproxy.ts detectPlatformAsset (line 417): add `else if (platform === 'win32') os = 'windows';` and derive the extension `const ext = os === 'windows' ? 'zip' : 'tar.gz';`, returning `CLIProxyAPI_${version}_${os}_${cpu}.${ext}`. Arch mapping (x64->amd64, arm64->aarch64) is already correct for the Windows asset names. Update tests/lib/cliproxy-platform-asset.test.ts: the line-31 assertion that win32/x64 is null FLIPS to expect /^CLIProxyAPI_[\d.]+_windows_amd64\.zip$/; add win32/arm64 -> /_windows_aarch64\.zip$/; keep win32/ia32 and darwin/ia32 -> null. See PRD W1 for exact before/after.

items.title: Given platform win32 and arch x64, detectPlatformAsset returns archive CLIProxyAPI_<ver>_windows_amd64.zip
Given platform win32 and arch arm64, detectPlatformAsset returns archive CLIProxyAPI_<ver>_windows_aarch64.zip
Given an unsupported combo (win32/ia32, darwin/ia32), detectPlatformAsset still returns null and linux/darwin combos still return .tar.gz names
getCliproxyBinary .exe suffix and win32-safe installed check

expected_outputs: cliproxy-windows-paths.test.ts passes covering getCliproxyBinary and isExecutableMode

narrative.Action: In src/lib/cliproxy.ts: (1) change getCliproxyBinary (line 61) to `getCliproxyBinary(platform: NodeJS.Platform = process.platform)` returning join(BIN_DIR, platform === 'win32' ? 'cliproxy.exe' : 'cliproxy') — existing zero-arg callers keep working. (2) Add exported pure helper `isExecutableMode(mode: number, platform: NodeJS.Platform = process.platform): boolean` returning `platform === 'win32' || (mode & 0o111) !== 0`, and use `st.isFile() && isExecutableMode(st.mode)` in isCliproxyInstalled (line 440). Create tests/lib/cliproxy-windows-paths.test.ts with unit tests for both helpers. See PRD W2.

items.title: getCliproxyBinary('win32') returns a path ending in cliproxy.exe while getCliproxyBinary('linux') returns a path ending in cliproxy with no suffix
isExecutableMode(0o644, 'win32') returns true; isExecutableMode(0o644, 'linux') returns false; isExecutableMode(0o755, 'linux') returns true
isCliproxyInstalled preserves existing linux behavior: a present file without any exec bit is reported as not installed on non-win32
Portable install: tar -xf, .exe extracted name, fs primitives

expected_outputs: typecheck and lint complete without errors
file-size guard passes (cliproxy.ts under 1000 lines or audited allowlist row)

narrative.Action: Change installCliproxySync (lines 495-527) and installCliproxyTask (lines 533-563) identically, keeping execSync in the Sync variant and execAsync in the Task variant (repo rule: no execSync in server-reachable code): (1) replace `tar -xzf` with `tar -xf` (GNU tar auto-detects gzip; Windows System32 bsdtar extracts zip); (2) add exported helper `extractedBinaryName(platform = process.platform)` returning 'cli-proxy-api.exe' on win32 else 'cli-proxy-api', use it for the extracted path; (3) replace the `install -m 0755` shell-out with rm(target, {force:true}) then copyFile(extracted, target) then chmod(target, 0o755) — rm-first is required or copyFile over a running binary throws ETXTBSY on linux; (4) replace `rm -rf tmpDir` with fs.rm(tmpDir, {recursive:true, force:true}) inside the existing non-fatal catch; (5) reword the unsupported-platform error to 'GPT subscription routing requires linux, darwin, or windows on amd64/arm64.' Sync variant uses rmSync/copyFileSync/chmodSync; Task variant uses fs/promises rm/copyFile/chmod. Do NOT add retry logic for EBUSY — all force-reinstall paths stop the proxy first. See PRD W3, D1, D4, H1.

items.title: Both install variants extract via 'tar -xf' (no -z flag) so the same command accepts .tar.gz on unix and .zip on Windows bsdtar
extractedBinaryName('win32') returns cli-proxy-api.exe and extractedBinaryName('linux') returns cli-proxy-api; install code joins tmpDir with this helper

When either install variant places the binary, it deletes the old target, copies the extracted file, and applies mode 0o755 via fs primitives; grep of src/lib/cliproxy.ts returns no 'install -m' or 'rm -rf' shell-outs
When detectPlatformAsset returns null the thrown message names linux, darwin, and windows (amd64/arm64) as supported, not 'linux and darwin only'
installCliproxyTask still contains no execSync calls (execAsync only), preserving the no-execSync-in-server rule
Version probe parses stdout when --version exits non-zero (all platforms)

expected_outputs: cliproxy-version-probe.test.ts passes covering parseCliproxyVersion and execFailureStdout

narrative.Action: In src/lib/cliproxy.ts: (1) export the existing parseCliproxyVersion (line 452), signature unchanged; (2) add exported helper `execFailureStdout(err: unknown): string` returning (err as {stdout?: string|Buffer})?.stdout?.toString() ?? '' — both execSync errors and promisified-exec rejections attach .stdout, and the sync probe's stdio ['ignore','pipe','ignore'] keeps stdout piped so it is present on the error; (3) in the catch blocks of isCliproxyUpToDateSync (line 474) and isCliproxyUpToDateTask (line 485), replace `return false` with `return parseCliproxyVersion(execFailureStdout(err)) === expectedCliproxyVersion();`; (4) update the doc comment (lines 457-465) to record that v7.2.113 does not define --version — it prints the banner to stdout and exits 2 — and that keeping the undefined flag is deliberate (banner + fast exit instead of starting a server). This fixes the silent ~65MB redownload on every cold start on linux/darwin too (verified locally: linux binary exits 2). Create tests/lib/cliproxy-version-probe.test.ts with pure tests, no child processes. See PRD W4, D2, D3.

items.title: parseCliproxyVersion('CLIProxyAPI Version: 7.2.113, Commit: bc71c77f, ...') returns '7.2.113' and parseCliproxyVersion('garbage') returns null
execFailureStdout returns the banner string from an Error carrying stdout as a string, round-trips a Buffer stdout, and falls back to '' when stdout is absent

Both isCliproxyUpToDate variants' catch blocks compare the version parsed from the failed exec's stdout against the pin instead of returning false unconditionally, so an installed pinned binary that exits 2 on --version no longer triggers a reinstall
isCliproxyRunningSync: netstat-based port probe on win32

expected_outputs: netstatShowsListener tests pass (LISTENING local port true, foreign-address-only false, empty false)

narrative.Action: In src/lib/cliproxy.ts isCliproxyRunningSync (lines 585-601): after the pidfile+isProcessAlive check, branch on process.platform === 'win32' to run execSync('netstat -ano -p TCP', {encoding:'utf8', stdio:'pipe', timeout:5000}) and return the result of a new exported pure helper `netstatShowsListener(output: string, port: number): boolean` — true only when a line contains LISTENING (case-insensitive word) AND a local address ending [:.]<port> followed by whitespace (a bare ':8317' substring would also match foreign addresses of ESTABLISHED rows). Non-win32 keeps the existing bash /dev/tcp probe byte-for-byte. Everything stays inside the existing try/catch that returns false on failure. This function is CLI-only, so execSync is permitted; the server-side isCliproxyRunningTask already uses portable net.connect and is untouched. Add fixture-based tests to tests/lib/cliproxy-windows-paths.test.ts. See PRD W5, D5.

items.title: netstatShowsListener returns true for a fixture line 'TCP 127.0.0.1:8317 0.0.0.0:0 LISTENING 1234' with port 8317
netstatShowsListener returns false when :8317 appears only as a foreign address on an ESTABLISHED row, and false for empty output
The non-win32 branch of isCliproxyRunningSync preserves the existing bash /dev/tcp probe unchanged
